item.title: Wendy’s worker wanted to quit, bosses funded his college; now he’s heading to Yale
item.description: Thalles Winner DeSouza, 23, is heading to Yale University after a difficult journey that began with surviving a shooting in Brazil. After moving to the US, he worked at Wendy’s while studying. His bosses helped fund three years of community college, supporting his education. DeSouza later transferred colleges and earned admission to Yale, where he plans to study political science and human rights on a pre-law track.

Wyoming buried 1,124 wind turbine blades; Missouri plant turns old blades into cement feedstock
item.description: Repurposing decommissioned wind turbine blades is becoming a promising trend, moving away from traditional landfill disposal. These large fiberglass structures are now being shredded and incorporated into cement production. Furthermore, innovative designs have led to the transformation of some blades into pedestrian bridges. While these initiatives are commendable, they signal just the beginning.

item.title: An 86-year-old geisha is turning to AI to protect Japan's falling geisha population
item.description: In a remarkable fusion of tradition and innovation, Japan's oldest geisha, Ikuko, incorporates hologram technology to safeguard her art. By utilizing AI, she is able to stage performances as younger versions of herself amid a concerning decline in geisha numbers in Tokyo. Embracing social media for recruitment, Ikuko pushes for collaborative performances and seeks governmental backing to rejuvenate this cherished cultural legacy.

item.title: Quote of the day by Malala Yousafzai: ‘One child, one teacher, one book and one pen can change the world’
item.description: Malala Yousafzai's powerful message highlights education's ability to change the world. A child's curiosity, guided by a teacher, fuels learning and progress. Books transmit knowledge across generations and vast distances. A pen empowers individuals to share their own unique ideas. These fundamental elements collectively shape individual lives and global societies.

item.title: Quote of the day by Marcus Aurelius: 'What stands in the way becomes the way'
item.description: Life's significant turning points often appear as problems and challenges. Dealing with difficulties can fundamentally alter a person's life direction. Stoic philosophy emphasizes responding constructively to unavoidable circumstances. Historical figures like Abraham Lincoln and Stephen Hawking exemplify this resilience. The obstacle itself can become an integral part of the journey.

item.title: William Arnold travelled 1,700 miles to a remote phone box and made 52 calls; the usage protected it for another year
item.description: William Arnold embarked on a mission to save a secluded phone box on a distant island. To meet Ofcom's operational requirements, he placed fifty-two calls, ensuring that the kiosk remains available for another year. His dedication underscores the vital role public call boxes play in isolated communities, urging others to engage with and support these local resources.

item.title: How a Massachusetts cranberry farm became a thriving wetland
item.description: A former cranberry farm in Plymouth, Massachusetts, has been transformed into a thriving freshwater wetland after restoration work began in 2010. The project restored 225 acres of wetland and more than three miles of stream habitat, removed dams and barriers, and brought back native plants and wildlife. Thousands of migratory fish, including alewife and blueback herring, returned to areas they had been unable to reach for more than 100 years.

item.title: She had no claims for 10 years. Then aerial photos put her insurance at risk
item.description: Texas homeowners are increasingly finding that insurance companies are using aerial images of their properties to assess risks and decide whether to renew policies. Insurers use satellite, aircraft and third-party imagery, with some companies using AI to analyse roofs and identify possible damage. While insurers say the technology is faster and more efficient, consumer advocates warn that outdated or inaccurate images can lead to wrong decisions.

item.title: When Steve Jobs called death ‘life’s best invention’
item.description: Steve Jobs' 2005 Stanford speech emphasized death as life's greatest invention. He urged graduates to live each day as if it were their last. Jobs advised them not to waste time living someone else's life. He stressed the importance of following one's heart and intuition. This profound message continues to resonate with millions worldwide.

item.title: Blueface faces backlash after controversial comment sparks heated clash with woman during viral livestream
item.description: Rapper Blueface ignited controversy during a recent livestream after a heated discussion about colorism with a woman. It all started when he praised her dark complexion, which led to a complex debate on racism within the Black community. As tensions rose, Blueface ultimately decided to ask the woman to exit his vehicle, prompting significant chatter across social media about his comments and their implications.
